title: Local rings of a smooth algebra over a field are regular
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset A$, the localization $A_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), final assertion, applied at every prime (a globally smooth finite-presentation algebra is finite type and smooth at each prime)

proof.text: (Setup and the fibre dimension.) Fix a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ and write $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. By [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] $A$ is a finitely presented $k$-algebra, $A\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$, so $A$ is a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]; and $k\to A$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], with $g=1\notin\mathfrak q$, since $A_1=A$ is a smooth $k$-algebra. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-dimension-differentials] gives that $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a finite-dimensional $\kappa$-vector space with $$\dim_{\kappa}\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. (This is the implication (1) $\Rightarrow$ (3) of the source, which reduces the final assertion to the case where (2) holds.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), proof lines 38629-38639 ((1) => (3), so (2) holds)

proof.text: (The algebraically closed field.) Let $K$ be an algebraic closure of $\kappa$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] with its field homomorphism $\psi:\kappa\to K$; $K$ is an algebraically closed field extension of $k$ through $k\to A\to\kappa\xrightarrow{\psi}K$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Put $A_K=K\otimes_kA$, a $K$-algebra through $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes1$, with $j:A\to A_K$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. If $a_1,\dots,a_n$ generate $A$ as a $k$-algebra (step 1), then $1\otimes a_1,\dots,1\otimes a_n$ generate $A_K$ as a $K$-algebra, since $\lambda\otimes p(a_1,\dots,a_n)=\lambda\,p(1\otimes a_1,\dots,1\otimes a_n)$ for a polynomial $p$ over $k$ and the $\lambda\otimes a$ span $A_K$; so $A_K$ is a finite type $K$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38646-38653

proof.text: (The point $\mathfrak m$ over $\mathfrak q$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (2), applied to the $k$-algebra maps $\mathrm{id}_K:K\to K$ and $A\to\kappa\xrightarrow{\psi}K$, there is a $k$-algebra map $\phi:A_K\to K$ with $\phi(\lambda\otimes a)=\lambda\,\psi(\bar a)$, $\bar a$ the image of $a$ in $\kappa$; it is the composite $A_K\to K\otimes_k\kappa\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_K\otimes\psi}K$ of the source. It is $K$-linear and surjective ($\phi(\lambda\otimes1)=\lambda$), so $\mathfrak m=\ker\phi$ is a maximal ideal of $A_K$, and the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=(A_K)_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak m(A_K)_{\mathfrak m}\cong A_K/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is identified with $K$ by $\phi$; in particular the composite $K\to A_K\to\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ of the structure map with the residue map is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras. Moreover $\phi(j(a))=\psi(\bar a)$ and $\psi$ is injective, so $j^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\{a:\bar a=0\}=\mathfrak q$: $\mathfrak m$ lies over $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38650-38660

proof.text: (Dimensions.) By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension] for $k\to K$, the finite type $k$-algebra $A$ and the prime $\mathfrak m$ of $A_K$ lying over $\mathfrak q$ (step 3), $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\dim_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}A_K)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]; that node writes $A\otimes_kK$, and the swap $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes a$ is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras compatible with the maps from $A$, so it carries the prime over $\mathfrak q$ to $\mathfrak m$ and induces a homeomorphism of spectra, which preserves dimensions at corresponding points. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring] for the field $K$, the finite type $K$-algebra $A_K$ (step 2) and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, $\dim_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}A_K)=\dim((A_K)_{\mathfrak m})$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Hence, with step 1, $$\dim((A_K)_{\mathfrak m})=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\dim_\kappa\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa,$$ a finite number.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38661-38665 (citing Lemma 00P4 lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension and Lemma 00OU lemma-dimension-closed-point-finite-type-field)

proof.text: (Differentials.) By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] for $k\to K$ and $k\to A$, $\Omega_{A_K/K}\cong A_K\otimes_A\Omega_{A/k}$ as $A_K$-modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Tensoring with $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=K$ over $A_K$ (step 3) and using associativity, $\Omega_{A_K/K}\otimes_{A_K}\kappa(\mathfrak m)\cong\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_AK$, where $A$ acts on $K$ through $\phi\circ j=\psi\circ(A\to\kappa)$; since this map factors through $\kappa$, $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_AK\cong(\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa)\otimes_\kappa K$, the extension of scalars along $\psi$ of the $\kappa$-vector space $V=\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa$. A basis $(e_i)$ of $V$ gives the basis $(e_i\otimes1)$ of $V\otimes_\kappa K$, so $$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak m)}\Omega_{A_K/K}\otimes_{A_K}\kappa(\mathfrak m)=\dim_\kappa\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa=\dim((A_K)_{\mathfrak m})$$ by step 4. (The source first shrinks $A$ to a principal localization on which $\Omega_{A/k}$ is generated by at most $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ elements; only the fibre dimension at $\mathfrak m$ is used below, and the equality above gives it directly.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38642-38648 and 38666-38670 (citing Lemma 00RV lemma-differentials-base-change)

proof.text: (The cotangent space of $(A_K)_{\mathfrak m}$; the regularity half of Lemma 00TS, (3) $\Rightarrow$ (1), through Lemma 00TR.) Put $R=(A_K)_{\mathfrak m}$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mR$ its maximal ideal and $\kappa'=R/\mathfrak n=\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; $R$ is a $K$-algebra through $K\to A_K\to R$, and $K\to\kappa'$ is an isomorphism (step 3). A field is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so $A_K$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (step 2) and $R$ is a Noetherian local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] for $K\to R$ and the ideal $\mathfrak n$, the sequence $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\xrightarrow{\delta}\kappa'\otimes_R\Omega_{R/K}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{\kappa'/K}\to0$, $\delta(a\bmod\mathfrak n^2)=1\otimes\mathrm da$, is exact. Since $K\to\kappa'$ is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras, $\Omega_{\kappa'/K}\cong\Omega_{K/K}=0$ (for $\lambda\in K$, $\mathrm d\lambda=\lambda\,\mathrm d1=0$ by the Leibniz rule and $K$-linearity of $\mathrm d$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), so $\delta$ is surjective. (b) $\delta$ is injective. Let $C=R/\mathfrak n^2$ and $\pi:C\to\kappa'$ the quotient map, a $K$-algebra map with kernel $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$, of square zero. Let $\sigma:\kappa'\to C$ be the composite of the inverse of the isomorphism $K\to\kappa'$ with the structure map $K\to C$; it is a $K$-algebra map with $\pi\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_{\kappa'}$ (since $K\to C\to\kappa'$ is $K\to\kappa'$). By [lem-weil-pbc-square-zero-section-conormal-retraction] for $K$, $C$, $\pi$, $\sigma$, the map $\delta_C:\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\to\kappa'\otimes_C\Omega_{C/K}$, $x\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dx$, is injective. The quotient map $q:R\to C$ induces the $\kappa'$-linear map $q_*:\kappa'\otimes_R\Omega_{R/K}\to\kappa'\otimes_C\Omega_{C/K}$, $1\otimes\mathrm db\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm d(q(b))$ (functoriality of $\Omega$, [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), and $q_*\circ\delta=\delta_C$ (both send $a\bmod\mathfrak n^2$ to $1\otimes\mathrm d(q(a))$). As $\delta_C$ is injective, so is $\delta$. Hence $\delta:\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\to\kappa'\otimes_R\Omega_{R/K}$ is an isomorphism of $\kappa'$-vector spaces. (In the source, Lemma 00TR proves this for every maximal ideal of a finite type algebra over an algebraically closed field, getting $\kappa'=K$ from the Nullstellensatz and the injectivity from the split sequence of Lemma 02HP; here $\kappa'=K$ holds by construction, step 3.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TS (lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar, line 38505), proof line 38525 ((1), (2), (3) equivalent by Lemma 00TR); Lemma Tag 00TR (lemma-rank-omega, line 38475) and its proof (exact sequence of Lemma 00RU lemma-differential-seq, split by Lemma 02HP lemma-differential-seq-split, Omega of kappa(m)/k = 0)

proof.text: ($(A_K)_{\mathfrak m}$ is regular.) By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] for $K\to A_K$ and the multiplicative set $A_K\setminus\mathfrak m$, $\Omega_{R/K}\cong(\Omega_{A_K/K})_{\mathfrak m}=\Omega_{A_K/K}\otimes_{A_K}R$ as $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], so $\kappa'\otimes_R\Omega_{R/K}\cong\Omega_{A_K/K}\otimes_{A_K}\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ by associativity of the tensor product. By steps 6 and 5, $$\dim_{\kappa'}\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak m)}\Omega_{A_K/K}\otimes_{A_K}\kappa(\mathfrak m)=\dim R .$$ By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] for the Noetherian local ring $R$ (step 6), $R=(A_K)_{\mathfrak m}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), lines 38674-38676 ('we know by Lemma 00TS that the local ring (S_K)_m is regular')

proof.text: (Flat descent of regularity.) By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] for $K/k$ and the $k$-algebra $A$, the map $A\to A\otimes_kK$ is faithfully flat, in particular flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]; composing with the swap isomorphism $A\otimes_kK\cong K\otimes_kA$, the map $j:A\to A_K$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (step 1) and $A_K$ by step 6. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] for $j$, the prime $\mathfrak m$ and $j^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q$ (step 3), the induced map $A_{\mathfrak q}\to(A_K)_{\mathfrak m}$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Since $(A_K)_{\mathfrak m}$ is a regular local ring (step 7), [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] gives that $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. As $\mathfrak q$ was arbitrary, this proves the statement.
